newsitem.title: USA: G10 endorses financial systems report.
newsitem.headline: G10 endorses financial systems report.

text.p: The Group of Ten countries said Monday that they endorsed a working party's report calling for a concerted international strategy to strengthen financial systems.

In a statement issued following the group's meeting, it said that the strategy calls for the development of an international consensus on key elements of a sound financial system and the formulation of sound principles and practices in crucial areas such as bank supervision and securities oversight.
The statement also said that the G10 saw no reason to set up formal mechanisms to deal with electronic money.
"They saw no need at this time to establish new formal international coordinating mechanisms specifically addressing electronic money developments," the statement said.
The statement also recommended that the articles of the International Monetary Fund be amended to reflect capital account liberalization.

"They affirmed that the liberalization of capital account transactions offer substantial economic benefits and should be supported by overall economic and structural policies fostering macroeconomic equilibrium and financial sector strength," the statement said.
The G10 is made up of Germany, France, Britain, Japan, the United States, Switzerland, the Netherlands, Canada, Belgium, Italy and Sweden.
They met in conjunction with the spring meetings of the IMF and World Bank.
